RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

You and the successful candidate are both men, so an all-male panel gives you no mechanism of disadvantage. Raising it would look like scattershot grievance-hunting and weaken the parts of your case that are genuinely strong.

Those parts are: a completed PhD versus an unfinished one, six papers versus two, four years of teaching — and a two-week silence on a request for written reasons. Public universities usually owe applicants reasons, and the appointment criteria should be documented.

So follow up in writing, cite the relevant appointment regulation, ask how "strong industry experience" was weighted against the published criteria, and set a deadline before escalating to the ombudsman or union.
